In summary, our research is concerned with

a general strategy for sequential resonance assignment of the proton NMR spectra of proteins, which is based on the use of short, non-covalent proton-proton distances between neighbouring residues in the protein sequence.
the application of 1H nuclear Overhauser spectroscopy to sequential assignments of protein resonance spectra.
the development of a new, general method for sequential assignments of protein proton resonance spectra.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in principle, sequential resonance assignments can be obtained in protein nuclear magnetic resonance spectra by measuring the short, non-bonds proton-proton distances.

the proton-proton distances between amide protons and protons of neighbouring amino acid residues, i.e. the sequential distances, should be the most reliable and generally applicable means to obtain individual resonance assignments in 1H nuclear Overhauser spectra of proteins.
, at present, the most promising approach to sequential resonance assignments is the use of through-space spin-probe experiments, which are based on short, non-bound proton-proton distances.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proton-proton distances between neighbouring residues in the protein sequence, which are allowed on the basis of the dihedral angle constraints of the Ramachandran map, are sufficiently short to be detectable by nuclear Overhausers.

the distances between amides of residues in a polypeptide chain, which correspond to sterically allowed values of the dihedral angle φi, are in general shorter than those between amide protons of residues which correspond to sterical allowed values of the angles ψi, and that the distances between Cα and Cα protons, which correspond to a sterical allowed values for χi1, are in general longer than the other proton-proton distances between neighbouring residues in the sequence.
the proton-proton distances between amide protons of neighbouring, as well as distant residues in the polypeptide chain are short enough to allow nuclear Overhauser effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the distances between amides and Cα and Cα and β carbons are short enough to allow for the detection of NOEs.
short, non-bonds proton-proton distances can be used for sequential resonance assignments in proteins.
short distance information between protons can be used for sequential resonance assignment.
